rationale: Two major test-coverage gaps found. (1) The normalization intentionally silences user-typed name changes when initial.name is empty — an accepted trade-off per the plan — but no unit test documents or pins this boundary, so a future narrowing of the condition would be undetected. (2) The new integration test only asserts the popup does NOT appear on an untouched form; no complementary test verifies the popup DOES appear when the user genuinely edits the form, meaning a fully disabled unsaved-changes guard would pass the suite. No-spec mode (no story/spec artifact): acceptance criteria audit not run; confidence forced to low. Commit subjects pass EPMCDME-XXXX format. No security issues. 2 dismiss (redundant condition style, fragile navigation target — low risk).

standards_review.notes: Both commits match EPMCDME-14129: Capital sentence — 'Exclude auto-generated name from datasource form dirty comparison' and 'Add regression test — no unsaved-changes popup on fresh datasource form'.
No secrets, injection surfaces, or auth-related changes in the diff.

findings.problem: No unit test pins the accepted trade-off that normalization silences user-typed name changes when initial.name is empty. The test file covers 'initial empty + auto-generated name → false' but not 'initial empty + user-typed name → false', leaving the boundary undocumented.
findings.impact: A future change narrowing the condition (e.g. only matching timestamp-format names) would break the bug fix without a failing test. More importantly, the data-loss scenario — user types a name on the create form then navigates away, no popup appears — is silent in the test suite.
findings.recommendation: Add a unit test to compareFormData.test.ts: compareFormData({ ...base, name: '' }, { ...base, name: 'user-typed-name' }) === false, with a comment naming the accepted trade-off (same as the plan's risk note).

findings.problem: The new integration test only checks the negative case (popup must NOT appear on untouched form). No test verifies the popup DOES appear when the user has made a genuine edit. The guard correctness is unverified from the integration-test level.
findings.impact: A regression that disables useUnsavedChangesWarning or useBlocker entirely would pass the complete new test suite without any failure. The fix is correct but the safety net is one-sided.
findings.recommendation: Add a companion integration test in the 'Unsaved Changes Guard' describe block: user edits a field (e.g. types in the description input), navigates away via router.navigate, and asserts the 'Unsaved Changes' heading IS in the document.
